name: French Expeditionary Army (Expédition Particulière)
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Yorktown : "army of 7,800 Frenchmen, 3,100 militia, and 8,000 Continentals" (Yorktown, late Sept 1781; includes troops from de Grasse's fleet). At Newport: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport,_Rhode_Island : "an army of 450 officers and 5,300 men" (July 1780); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exp%C3%A9dition_Particuli%C3%A8re : "it numbered up to 5,500 troops".

rows.label: Newport (lands with the army)
rows.quote: He landed at Newport, Rhode Island, on 10 July
rows.note: Other sources (Expédition Particulière article, NPS timeline) give July 11 for the fleet's arrival; July 10 per the Rochambeau and Newport articles.

rows.label: Wethersfield conference with Washington
rows.quote: On May 23 and 24, Washington and Rochambeau held a conference at Wethersfield
rows.note: Joseph Webb House article calls it a five-day conference; Yorktown campaign article dates it May 23-24.

rows.label: Leaves Newport with his staff
rows.quote: Rochambeau and his general staff left Newport on June 10, 1781

rows.label: Providence (army assembles, review June 16)
rows.quote: arriving at Providence the following day

rows.label: Waterman Tavern, Coventry (first division)
rows.quote: Rochambeau left with the first division (the Bourbonnais Regiment)
rows.note: Evening of June 18 at Waterman Tavern per same article.

rows.label: Asa Barnes Tavern, Southington
rows.quote: Rochambeau and his officers stayed at the Asa Barnes Tavern
rows.note: Date is the army's eighth camp (June 26) in the same article; first division, with which he marched, arrived that day.

rows.label: Israel Bronson Tavern, Middlebury
rows.quote: Rochambeau and his officers were entertained at the Israel Bronson Tavern
rows.note: First division stayed the night of June 27 at Breakneck Hill per same article.

rows.label: Odell farm HQ, Philipsburg camp (Greenburgh)
rows.quote: The Odell farm served as Rochambeau's headquarters from 6 July to 18 August 1781.
rows.note: Headquarters stayed at the Philipsburg camp until the army left in late August.

rows.label: Meets Washington at Chester
rows.quote: They met at Chester, Pennsylvania, where Washington shared the news
rows.note: Article says both left Philadelphia 'by September 5'; Rochambeau went by boat on the Delaware. Date approximate (+/-1 day).

rows.label: Mount Vernon (day after Washington)
rows.quote: Rochambeau and his staff arrived the following day
rows.note: Washington arrived Sept 9 per the same article.

rows.label: Williamsburg (arrives with Washington)
rows.quote: arrived in Williamsburg, Virginia, on September 14
rows.note: Both commanders; Siege of Yorktown article also gives Sept 14 for Washington.

rows.label: Siege of Yorktown (surrender, British offer sword to him first)
rows.quote: O'Hara first attempted to surrender to Rochambeau
rows.note: Rochambeau is also a signatory of the articles of capitulation signed Oct 19. No source fetched places him personally at Yorktown on Sept 28; only the surrender day is stated.

rows.label: Newburgh HQ, last meeting with Washington
rows.quote: The Count de Rochambeau, who arrived here this morning
rows.note: Quote is Washington's letter of Dec 7, 1782; Rochambeau was returning to Philadelphia to sail for France.
